section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch2 — Piaget's Cognitive Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A Class-2 child insists a tall thin glass holds more juice than a short wide glass, even after watching the same juice poured between them. Which Piagetian limitation does this show?

options.option_text: Lack of conservation, dominated by centration on height
Loss of reversibility due to over-assimilation

explanation: In the pre-operational stage the child centres on one salient dimension (height) and cannot conserve quantity. Object permanence is an earlier sensorimotor achievement; hypothetico-deductive reasoning belongs to formal operations.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch2 — Piaget's Cognitive Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: According to Piaget, the ability to perform mental operations on concrete objects but not yet on abstract, hypothetical propositions is characteristic of children aged approximately:
explanation: The concrete operational stage (7–11) allows logical operations on tangible things but not abstract hypotheticals, which appear in the formal operational stage (11+).

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch2 — Piaget's Cognitive Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A toddler who calls every four-legged animal 'dog' finally learns to call a cat 'cat' after correction. Adjusting the existing schema to admit this new category is, in Piaget's terms:
explanation: Assimilation fits new input into an existing schema (calling the cat 'dog'); accommodation modifies the schema to fit reality (a separate 'cat' schema).

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch3 — Vygotsky's Sociocultural Theory
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: The gap between what a child can do alone and what the same child can do with guidance from a more capable person is Vygotsky's:
explanation: The ZPD is the distance between actual developmental level (independent problem solving) and potential level (with guidance). Instruction should target this zone.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch3 — Vygotsky's Sociocultural Theory
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A teacher gives strong hints at first and gradually withdraws them as the pupil masters long division. This temporary, tapering support is called:
explanation: Scaffolding is graduated help within the ZPD that is reduced as competence grows. Associated with Vygotsky (term coined by Wood, Bruner & Ross).

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch3 — Vygotsky's Sociocultural Theory
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A key contrast between Piaget and Vygotsky on the role of language and thought is that:

options.option_text: For Piaget thought largely precedes language, whereas for Vygotsky language is a tool that shapes and advances thought
Both held that language and thought develop in complete independence of each other
For Piaget social speech is the origin of all reasoning, unlike Vygotsky
Vygotsky denied any role for social interaction in cognitive growth

explanation: Piaget saw egocentric speech as a by-product of immature thought; Vygotsky saw private/social speech as the very instrument through which higher thought develops.
